children: Local Bounti's sales rose 1% year over year, while its net loss narrowed 36%. Higher production and sales from Georgia, Texas and Washington were partly offset by lower club-customer volumes and reduced consumer demand for lettuce and salad products following the Cyclospora outbreak; lower R&D and G&A expenses also contributed to the narrower loss.
¹ Reported as “Sales”. ² Reported as “Net loss attributable to common stockholders”. ³ Reported as “Basic and diluted”.
: Supply agreements for butterhead lettuce from California and Texas were extended with a national retailer through 2Q 2028.
: Brookshire Brothers launched in about 66 stores; Albertsons' Denver division launched in about 110 stores.
: In September, Local Bounti added baby leaf listings in Idaho, Oregon and Texas, with shipments beginning in October.
: Year to date, G&A salaries, benefits and payroll-related expenses fell $1.7M year over year; more efficient seeding lowered seed costs.
: Georgia, Texas and Washington facilities' processes matured, shifting costs from R&D to cost of goods sold.
